jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Compute Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation of models. We provide a unified platform for OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads.

Our work spans cloud providers, bare metal infrastructure, data centers, and the foundational services that make compute usable. We partner across Engineering, Research, Product, Capacity Planning, Finance, and Data Center Infrastructure to bring new capacity online and support OpenAI’s growing compute needs.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

About the Role

As a Technical Program Manager for Compute Infrastructure, you will own the supply signal for all GPUs entering our fleet: a reliable view of what capacity is arriving, where and when it will arrive, and when it is expected to become usable. You will own the roadmap, requirements, delivery, and adoption of the tools, data, and platform behind that signal, partnering with Engineering to build systems that support planning and execution across OpenAI.

You will also lead programs that turn incoming supply into usable compute. Working across cloud providers, Data Center Infrastructure, and compute engineering teams, you will connect physical site readiness with the CPU, storage, network, GPU, and foundational services required to bring new sites and clusters online.

You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, managing a broad portfolio of infrastructure programs and making dependencies, risks, and decisions clear from working teams through leadership. Your work will help teams plan with confidence, respond to supply changes, and deliver capacity on time.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the GPU supply signal across the fleet. Maintain a trusted view of incoming capacity across providers, sites, and clusters, including quantities, delivery forecasts, acceptance and readiness milestones, and expected dates for production use. Make changes and their downstream effects visible.

  • Build and scale the tools, data, and platform behind that signal. Own the roadmap, requirements, delivery, and adoption, partnering with Engineering on data models, integrations, quality checks, and planning workflows. Serve Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside Finance, Accounting, leadership, Engineering, and Research.

  • Connect supply with capacity planning. Partner with Capacity Planning on supply and demand management, allocation planning, and scenario analysis. Ensure plans reflect current supply forecasts, infrastructure constraints, and the effects of early or late deliveries.

  • Coordinate physical readiness for new capacity. Work closely with Data Center Infrastructure and cloud service providers to align ready-for-service dates, site construction, power and cooling readiness, supply-chain convergence, equipment delivery, and commissioning. Track dependencies and drive resolution of gaps that threaten deployment.

  • Lead logical readiness across infrastructure resources. Coordinate CPU, storage, network, GPU, Kubernetes, and dependent compute foundation services so new clusters can support their intended workloads. Make clear which missing services or resources could delay GPU use.

  • Drive deployment across cloud and bare metal environments. Lead integrated plans across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure partners, accounting for provider-specific dependencies while establishing consistent readiness criteria and handoffs.

  • Establish Delivery Scorecards for cloud providers and internal infrastructure teams. Track delivery commitments, forecast changes, actual delivery, readiness milestones, and time to usable capacity. Use these scorecards to identify recurring gaps, clarify recovery actions, and improve delivery predictability.

  • Improve the reliability and repeatability of cluster bringup. Partner with Engineering to scale automation, runbooks, validation, and deployment processes. Reduce manual coordination and the time between capacity delivery and production use.

  • Manage the critical paths across concurrent programs. Establish clear milestones, owners, dependencies, and escalation paths. Resolve cross-team blockers and drive decisions that keep site and cluster deployments moving.

  • Communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs clearly. Give technical and business stakeholders the information they need to understand capacity availability, assess changes to the plan, and make timely decisions.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience leading major technical programs, including compute infrastructure, hyperscaler deployments, capital projects, or similarly complex infrastructure work.

  • Possess a degree in a hard science or engineering discipline, or have a demonstrated track record of equivalent engineering expertise.

  • Are familiar with Kubernetes deployments and have worked with at least one major cloud provider—such as AWS, GCP, Azure, or OCI—to scale compute infrastructure. Experience coordinating deployments across multiple providers is valuable.

  • Are familiar with bare metal GPU capacity and the provisioning, inventory, and planning systems used to bring it into service.

  • Have worked with Capacity Planning teams on supply and demand management, allocations, constraints, and supporting tools. You understand how changes in delivery or readiness affect downstream capacity plans.

  • Have experience defining requirements for operational data and internal platforms. You can work with engineers to establish useful data models, improve data quality, and build tools that teams adopt and rely on.

  • Understand how site readiness, power and cooling, equipment delivery, commissioning, and ready-for-service milestones affect cluster deployment. You can coordinate these dependencies without losing sight of when the intended workload can run.

  • Have a record of owning and delivering complex technical programs across internal teams and external partners, including cloud providers, equipment suppliers, or data center infrastructure teams.

  • Are technically adept and comfortable working with Engineering and Research to understand dependencies, evaluate tradeoffs, and turn complex problems into executable plans.

  • Build simple, scalable processes and communicate clearly with both technical teams and business stakeholders. You are resourceful in ambiguous environments and follow issues through to resolution.

  • Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link.

OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy

At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

jobs.title: Research Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
By applying to this role, you will be considered for Research Engineer roles across all teams at OpenAI.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer here, you will be responsible for building AI systems that can perform previously impossible tasks or achieve unprecedented levels of performance. We're looking for people with solid engineering skills (for example designing, implementing, and improving a massive-scale distributed machine learning system), writing bug-free machine learning code, and building the science behind the algorithms employed. 

The most outstanding deep learning results are increasingly attained at a massive scale, and these results require engineers who are comfortable working in large distributed systems. We expect engineering to play a key role in most major advances in AI of the future.

We expect you to:

  • Have strong programming skills

  • Have experience working in large distributed systems

  • Be excited about OpenAI’s approach to research 

Nice to have: 

  • Interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AI technology

  • Past experience in creating high-performance implementations of deep learning algorithms

jobs.title: Researcher, Safety Training
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.

About the Role


We are seeking researchers to advance safety training for OpenAI’s models. You will develop methods that improve model behavior after pretraining, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, preference optimization, adversarial training, synthetic data generation, safety evaluations, and model behavior analysis.

This role is highly cross-functional. You will work with core training teams, product teams, policy, legal, trust and safety, and domain experts to identify risks, design interventions, train models, evaluate outcomes, and launch safety improvements in OpenAI products.

In this role, you will:

  • Conduct research on safety post-training methods, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, adversarial training, synthetic data, and scalable oversight

  • Develop and implement model training interventions that make models safer, more reliable, and more aligned with user intent

  • Build evaluations and measurement infrastructure for safety harms, high-stakes reliability failures, policy adherence, jailbreak robustness, multimodal risks, agent behavior, and domain-specific risks

  • Translate ambiguous safety problems into concrete research plans, datasets, training runs, evals, and product-facing improvements

  • Analyze model failures such as hallucination, unsafe tool use, prompt injection, privacy leakage, over-refusal, under-refusal, sycophancy, and deceptive or misleading behavior

  • Partner with domain experts to design safety training approaches for areas like cyber, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, and other frontier-risk domains

  • Collaborate with research and deployment teams to ensure safety improvements are incorporated into OpenAI’s core model training and product launches

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training language models, multimodal models, or agentic systems

  • Have experience with RL, RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, preference optimization, instruction tuning, or related post-training methods

  • Care deeply about shaping model behavior in real-world systems, not only publishing research

  • Are excited by open-ended safety problems where the right method, dataset, eval, or training objective may not be obvious at the start

  • Bring strong research judgment and strong engineering ability, including comfort running experiments, analyzing model behavior, and working with large-scale ML systems

  • Have experience in one or more relevant domains: agents, tool use, multimodal models, cyber/security, reliability, uncertainty calibration, factuality, evals, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, or applied alignment

  • Enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, product, policy, legal, and trust and safety teams

  • Hold a PhD in machine learning, computer science, or a related field, or have equivalent practical research or engineering experience

Nice to have:

  • Experience improving production model behavior through post-training or deployment feedback

  • Experience building safety evals, automated graders, red-teaming systems, or monitoring pipelines

  • Experience working with human feedback, expert feedback, synthetic data, or policy-grounded training data

  • Experience in safety-critical or abuse-sensitive domains where models must balance helpfulness, refusal, uncertainty, and user intent

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Scaled Abuse
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Applied team safely brings OpenAI's technology to the world. We released ChatGPT; Plugins; DALL·E; and the APIs for GPT-5, embeddings, and fine-tuning. We also operate inference infrastructure at scale. There's a lot more on the immediate horizon.

Our customers build fast-growing businesses around our APIs, which power product features that were never before possible. ChatGPT is a prime example of what is currently possible. We simultaneously ensure that our powerful tools are used responsibly. Safe deployment is more important to us than unfettered growth.

The Fraud Engineering team works within our Applied Engineering organization identifying and responding to fraudsters on our platform. We are looking for a software engineer with anti fraud & abuse experience to help architect and build our next-generation anti-fraud systems.

About the role

The Scaled Abuse team protects OpenAI’s products and customers by detecting, preventing, and responding to fraudulent and abusive behavior at scale. We build and operate the backend and data systems that power real-time detection, investigation workflows, and enforcement — balancing strong protections with a great user experience as the platform grows.

Our work sits at the intersection of engineering and abuse expertise: we partner closely with Trust & Safety, Security, and Product to understand emerging attack patterns, translate messy signals into clear system behavior, and continuously harden our defenses. The problems are dynamic and ambiguous by default, so we value engineers who can quickly dive into an unfamiliar codebase, develop strong intuition about how it works end-to-end, and propose pragmatic improvements that make the entire stack more resilient.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build systems for fraud detection and remediation while balancing fraud loss, cost of implementation, and customer experience

  • Work closely with finance, security, product, research, and trust & safety operations to holistically combat fraudulent and abusive actors on our system

  • Stay abreast of the latest techniques and tools to stay several steps ahead of determined and well resourced adversaries

  • Utilize GPT-5 and future models to more effectively combat fraud and abuse

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have at least 5 years of software engineering experience in backend and data systems.

  • Have at least 2 years experience in fraud or abuse analysis, investigation, and/or operations

  • Can dive into our codebase, intuit how it works, and be able to have a strong intuition for suggestions that will lead us to a stronger engineering position.

  • A voracious and intrinsic desire to learn and fill in missing skills. An equally strong talent for sharing that information clearly and concisely with others

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing conditions. You view changes as an opportunity to add structure and order when necessary

  • Experience in Machine Learning techniques is a plus, but not required

Our tech stack

Our infrastructure is built on Terraform, Kubernetes, Azure, Python, Postgres, and Kafka. While we value experience with these technologies, we are primarily looking for engineers with strong technical skills and the ability to quickly pick up new tools and frameworks.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Data Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Data Platform at OpenAI owns the foundational data stack powering critical product, research, and analytics workflows. We operate some of the largest Spark compute fleets in production; design, and build data lakes and metadata systems on Iceberg and Delta with a vision toward exabyte-scale architecture; run high throughput streaming platforms on Kafka and Flink; provide orchestration with Airflow; and support ML feature engineering tooling such as Chronon. Our mission is to deliver reliable, secure, and efficient data access at scale and accelerate intelligent, AI assisted data workflows.

Join us to build and operate these core platforms that underpin OpenAI products, research, and analytics.

We’re not just scaling infrastructure – we’re redefining how people interact with data. Our vision includes intelligent interfaces and AI-assisted workflows that make working with data faster, more reliable, and more intuitive.

About the Role

This role focuses on building and operating data infrastructure that supports massive compute fleets and storage systems, designed for high performance and scalability. You’ll help design, build, and operate the next generation of data infrastructure at OpenAI. You will scale and harden big data compute and storage platforms, build and support high-throughput streaming systems, build and operate low latency data ingestions, enable secure and governed data access for ML and analytics, and design for reliability and performance at extreme scale.

You will take full lifecycle ownership: architecture, implementation, production operations, and on-call participation.

You’ve supported Spark, Kafka, Flink, Airflow, Trino, or Iceberg as platforms. You’re well-versed in infrastructure tooling like Terraform, experienced in debugging large-scale distributed systems, and excited about solving data infrastructure problems in the AI space.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and maintain data infrastructure systems such as distributed compute, data orchestration, distributed storage, streaming infrastructure, machine learning infrastructure while ensuring scalability, reliability, and security

  • Ensure our data platform can scale by orders of magnitude while remaining reliable and efficient

  • Accelerate company productivity by empowering your fellow engineers & teammates with excellent data tooling and systems

  • Collaborate with product, research and analytics teams to build the technical foundations capabilities that unlock new features and experiences

  • Own the reliability of the systems you build, including participation in an on-call rotation for critical incidents

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 4+ years in data infrastructure engineering OR

  • Have 4+ years in infrastructure engineering with a strong interest in data

  • Take pride in building and operating scalable, reliable, secure systems

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change

  • Have an intrinsic desire to learn and fill in missing skills, and an equally strong talent for sharing learnings clearly and concisely with others

This role is exclusively based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.
